cases.prompt: Review this application module against Google's Rust guide. The enclosing service uses Tokio; this is an ordinary Cargo project outside Google. Preserve behavior and report only actionable findings.
Review this worker code against Google's Rust guide. Workers must share the same potentially large allocation and run on separate threads; keep this behavior.
Review this internal application helper using Google's Rust guide. Callers pass slices and immediately index the returned vector; do not change the public signature for hypothetical reuse.
Review this not-yet-released reusable library API using Google's Rust guide. Callers include &str and String owners. Suggest a compatible input shape and explain why.
Review this application configuration loader against Google's Rust guide. A missing or unreadable file is an expected user-facing error. A signature change is allowed.
Review the panic policy in this private application helper against Google's Rust guide. The vector is constructed nonempty immediately before last(); no recoverable error is involved.
Review this released library options type against Google's Rust guide. External callers use Options { retries: 2, ..Default::default() }; preserve that construction pattern.

Review these two new library enums against Google's Rust guide before release. Visibility is deliberately permanently binary. Event is used across teams and will gain variants; we cannot update all callers together.
Review imports against Google's Rust guide. Identify which wildcard imports require changes and which may stay. Test-local and enum-local imports should be assessed in context.

Suggest Google Rust formatting checks for this stable-only Cargo project. Retain its pinned toolchain and existing max_width. Explain what to do with unsupported rustfmt options; do not write configuration.
Review this API for correctness and Google's unsafe-code guidance. Empty slices are valid inputs. Suggest a safe design; a signature change is allowed.

Using Google's Rust guide, should this application type gain a Render trait merely to keep rendering methods in a separate group? There is no generic dispatch, dynamic dispatch, foreign type, or second implementation.
Review this first-party Chromium module against Google's Rust guide. It runs in Chromium's existing task system. Identify applicable concurrency policy issues; do not invent replacement APIs.
Review this module against Google's Rust guide within the supplied project policy. Keep existing call sites and configuration. Explain any conflict instead of silently changing policy.
Fix the Python dictionary lookup so an unknown language returns None. The string 'rust' is just a key; no Rust code or style review is involved.
